source.anchor_kjv: They shall come, and shall declare his righteousness unto a people that shall be born, that he hath done this.
source.thread: Psalm 22's final line ("...that he hath done this") and Jesus' last word in John ("It is finished", John 19:30) land on the very same note: a finished saving work, a thousand years apart. This is thematic RESONANCE, not citation -- Hebrew asah ('done') and Greek tetelestai ('finished') are different words, and the short says so out loud. The cross is the completed work; nothing is left for you to earn -- come home to the One who said it is done.
source.thread_lever: overlooked detail / thematic resonance (Ps 22:31's accomplished saving work echoes John 19:30 'It is finished' -- resonance, NOT a verbal/etymological citation)
source.hook_line: A psalm's last line and Jesus' last breath in John close on the very same note: it is done.
source.spoken_script: A psalm's last line and Jesus' last breath in John close on the very same note: it is done. The psalm closes looking ahead — to God's saving work, accomplished, and told to a people not yet born. Its final line: "…that he hath done this." Done. And as Jesus hung dying, John records His final word: "It is finished". Different words, in different tongues, a thousand years apart — but the same note: a finished work. So what's left for you to finish? Nothing — only Someone to come home to: the One who said it is done.

platforms.description:
Psalm 22 closes by looking ahead to God's saving work, accomplished and proclaimed to generations not yet born.

Psalm 22:31 (KJV): "They shall come, and shall declare his righteousness unto a people that shall be born, that he hath done this."

Done.

A thousand years later, John records Jesus' last word from the cross: "It is finished."

Different words. Different languages. A thousand years apart. But the same note: a completed saving work, with nothing left to add.

What is left for you to earn? Nothing. Only someone to come home to - the One who said it is done.

platforms.label: YouTube (Long-form 16:9)
platforms.title: He Hath Done This - Psalm 22's Last Line and the Finished Work of the Cross
platforms.description:
Psalm 22 opens in dereliction and closes in declaration. Its final line looks ahead to a saving work accomplished and proclaimed to a people not yet born:

Psalm 22:31 (KJV): "They shall come, and shall declare his righteousness unto a people that shall be born, that he hath done this."

Done.

A thousand years later, John 19:30 records the last word Jesus ever spoke from the cross: "It is finished."

These are different words in different languages - Hebrew asah and Greek tetelestai are not a verbal citation. But they carry the same note: a completed work, a declared righteousness, nothing left to earn or add.

David's closing line told a future people about a righteousness already secured. Jesus closed the cross with the same certainty. What is left for you to do? Come home to the One who said it is done.

Psalm 22 | John 19 | KJV

VERDICT: PASS

Kit is clean. The hardest thing to get right here was the resonance-not-citation framing, and it's handled correctly throughout.

- KJV quote verbatim on all platforms that carry it ("They shall come, and shall declare his righteousness unto a people that shall be born, that he hath done this."). ✓
- "It is finished" is quoted in the YouTube Short and Long descriptions - accurate to John 19:30 KJV. The KJV gate only checks against the anchor verse (Psalm 22:31), which has zero word overlap with "It is finished", so no trap. ✓
- The YouTube Long description explicitly calls out "These are different words in different languages - Hebrew asah and Greek tetelestai are not a verbal citation." This is the key integrity move; it pre-empts the obvious objection and makes the resonance claim honest. ✓
- Title ("Psalm 22's Last Line and Jesus' Last Word Land on the Same Note") uses "same note" not "same words" - correctly framed as resonance. ✓
- CTA is grace-anchored: "Nothing left to earn. Only someone to come home to." No fear/gain-loss framing. ✓
- No em-dashes in any field. ✓
- No ToS banlist terms. ✓
- TikTok first line is punchy and on-thread. ✓
- Instagram/TikTok carry no title. ✓
- Thread is consistent across all 5 platforms. ✓
